spec.title: Uptime
spec.description: Time since boot.

spec.title: CPU busy
spec.description: Share of CPU time not spent idle, averaged over all cores.

spec.title: Memory used
spec.description: Excludes cache and buffers — this is what the box would miss if it went away.

spec.title: Root filesystem used
spec.description: A full root here takes out ACME renewals and the journal before it takes out nginx.

spec.title: Requests/s
spec.description: From nginx's own counter, which includes requests the access log never reaches — rejected connections and requests closed before a response line.

spec.title: Nebula tunnels
spec.description: Established tunnels in the main hostmap. As a lighthouse this counts the nodes that have handshaked with this host, not everything on the mesh.

spec.title: Active connections
spec.description: Open client connections, including keep-alive idlers. The one thing the access log cannot reconstruct after the fact.

spec.title: 5xx responses
spec.description: Server errors in the selected range, across every vhost matching the picker.

spec.title: Requests logged
spec.description: Access-log lines in the selected range.

spec.title: DNS queries/s
spec.description: Every query blocky answered, over DoT, DoH and plain DNS together.

spec.title: Nebula certificate
spec.description: Time left on this host's mesh certificate. Nothing renews it automatically; when it lapses the host drops off the overlay and takes its reverse proxy with it.

spec.title: Responses/s by status class
spec.description: Parsed from the access log, so it counts responses rather than requests: anything nginx dropped before writing a status line is in the Requests/s stat and not here.

spec.expr: sum(count_over_time({nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | status >= 300 | status < 400 [5m])) / 300
sum(count_over_time({nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | status >= 400 | status < 500 [5m])) / 300

spec.title: WAN traffic
spec.description: Inbound positive, outbound mirrored below zero.

spec.title: Request duration
spec.description: Quantiles over $request_time, which is measured from the first byte read from the client to the last byte written back — slow clients inflate it as much as slow upstreams do.

spec.expr: quantile_over_time(0.5, {nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | unwrap duration | __error__="" [5m])
quantile_over_time(0.9, {nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | unwrap duration | __error__="" [5m])
quantile_over_time(0.99, {nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | unwrap duration | __error__="" [5m])

spec.title: CPU and memory
spec.description: Load average against core count, with memory used for scale.

spec.title: Responses/s by vhost
spec.description: Split by the server block that matched, not by the Host header the client sent — aliases of one vhost land on one line here. The Top vhosts table below splits by requested name.

spec.title: 4xx and 5xx per vhost
spec.description: Which vhost the errors are coming from.

spec.expr: sum by (server) (count_over_time({nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | status >= 400 | status < 500 [5m])) / 300
sum by (server) (count_over_time({nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | status >= 500 [5m])) / 300

spec.title: Bytes served
spec.description: Response body bytes only; headers and TLS overhead are not counted, so this reads lower than the WAN counter.

spec.expr: sum(rate({nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | unwrap bytes | __error__="" [5m]))

spec.title: Upstream response time
spec.description: Only requests that were proxied — the static vhosts log an empty upstream time and are dropped by the unwrap. A gap between this and total request duration is time spent on this host or on the client's link, not on oreamnos.

spec.expr: quantile_over_time(0.5, {nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | upstream_time != "" | unwrap upstream_time | __error__="" [5m])
quantile_over_time(0.95, {nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | upstream_time != "" | unwrap upstream_time | __error__="" [5m])
quantile_over_time(0.99, {nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | upstream_time != "" | unwrap upstream_time | __error__="" [5m])

spec.title: nginx connection states
spec.description: Waiting is idle keep-alive. Reading climbing while writing stays flat is the shape of a slowloris; writing climbing is a slow or stuck upstream.

spec.title: Connections accepted vs handled
spec.description: The two counters differ only when nginx drops a connection it accepted, which means it hit worker_connections or a resource limit. Any daylight between the lines is a configuration problem, not load.

spec.title: Rate limiting and rejections
spec.description: 429 is this host's own limit_req/limit_conn zones biting; 499 is the client hanging up before nginx answered. Both are worth watching after a limit change.

spec.title: Top requested names
spec.description: By the Host header, so the aliases on a shared vhost show separately.

spec.expr: topk(15, sum by (vhost) (count_over_time({nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" [$__range])))

spec.title: Top paths
spec.description: Normalised request path ($uri), so the query string is not part of the grouping.

spec.expr: topk(15, sum by (uri) (count_over_time({nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" [$__range])))

spec.title: Top clients
spec.description: Source addresses as nginx saw them. This host is the edge, so these are real remote addresses and not a proxy's.

spec.expr: topk(15, sum by (remote) (count_over_time({nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" [$__range])))

spec.title: Top failing paths
spec.description: 4xx and 5xx grouped by path and status, which is where a broken proxy target or a missing asset shows up first.

spec.expr: topk(15, sum by (uri, status) (count_over_time({nodename="hisn", source="nginx.service", server=~"${vhost:regex}"} | json | __error__="" | status >= 400 [$__range])))

spec.title: Error responses
spec.description: Every 4xx and 5xx access line, newest first.

spec.title: Tunnels
spec.description: Peers in the main hostmap.

spec.title: Pending handshakes
spec.description: Peers this host is trying to reach and has not completed a handshake with. Steady non-zero means something is unreachable, not busy.

spec.title: Relay indexes
spec.description: Tunnels this host is relaying for other nodes, which it does because it is a lighthouse.

spec.title: Certificate expiry
spec.description: Same value as the Overview tile, repeated here because it is a nebula fact.

spec.title: Handshake timeouts/s
spec.description: Handshakes abandoned after retries. A node that cannot be reached at all produces a steady trickle here.

spec.title: Version
spec.description: Reported by the running binary, not by the package set.

spec.title: Hostmap
spec.description: Tunnel and index counts. Indexes exceed hosts when a peer has more than one tunnel open, which is normal during a rehandshake and not otherwise.

spec.title: Handshakes
spec.description: Initiated against timed out. Both counters are cumulative gauges — nebula exports every counter that way — so these are rates taken over them.

spec.title: Message rates
spec.description: Every nebula message type this host sends and receives. `message` is tunnelled payload; the rest is control traffic, and on a lighthouse the lighthouse and punchy lines are the bulk of it.

spec.title: Lighthouse queries
spec.description: Host queries answered and sent. This is the work being a lighthouse actually costs, and it is the metric that moves when a node cannot find a peer.

spec.title: Firewall drops
spec.description: Packets the nebula firewall rejected, by reason. no_rule on the inbound side is a peer sending something the rules in modules/personal/networking/nebula.nix do not allow — worth reading before widening a rule.

spec.title: UDP socket
spec.description: Kernel-side view of nebula's own socket. Drops and a growing backlog mean the host is not reading fast enough, which is a different failure from a peer being unreachable.

spec.title: Overlay traffic
spec.description: Bytes across the sifr0 tun device: the payload side of the mesh, as opposed to the message counts above. Inbound positive, outbound mirrored.

spec.title: Nebula log
spec.description: Handshake failures and certificate complaints land here first.

spec.title: Queries/s
spec.description: All protocols together: plain DNS on the mesh, DoT on 853 and DoH through nginx.

spec.title: Blocked share
spec.description: Queries answered from a blocklist rather than an upstream.

spec.title: Cache hit rate
spec.description: Share of lookups served from blocky's cache. Prefetching keeps popular names warm, so a high number here is the configuration working rather than a quiet resolver.

spec.title: Cache entries
spec.description: Names currently held in cache.

spec.title: Responses/s by type
spec.description: BLOCKED, CACHED, RESOLVED and the rest, as blocky classifies them.

spec.title: Response latency
spec.description: Quantiles from blocky's own histogram, split by response type: BLOCKED and CACHED answers are near-instant, so a rise in the aggregate is upstream latency.

spec.title: Cache and prefetch
spec.description: Prefetches are lookups blocky made on its own to keep a popular name warm; prefetch hits are the queries that then landed on a warm entry.

spec.title: Errors and list refreshes
spec.description: Failed downloads are blocklists that could not be fetched, which leaves the previous copy in place — the resolver keeps working while quietly going stale, so this is worth an eye.

spec.title: Query log
spec.description: blocky's own lines from the journal. Every resolver on the public internet can reach dns.huma.id, so the clients here are not necessarily anything of the user's.

spec.name: ds_prometheus
spec.label: Prometheus
spec.description: Prometheus data source holding this host's metrics.

spec.name: vhost
spec.label: Vhost
spec.description: nginx server blocks seen in the access log. Requires server to be a Loki label, which the o11y client sets from the JSON access line.
